draft_reply.body:
Daniel,

Following up on our claim for PRO BLF-77209115 (BOL BOL-884219). We've reviewed BlueLine's offer of $7,225.00 covering the missing carton and the nine accepted damaged units, and we'd like to move this forward with a counter-offer of $11,920.00, along with responses to the open items on our end.

On the five damaged units still in dispute: the signed proof of delivery documents all five damaged cartons at the time of delivery, and the independent inspection report from Southwest Cargo Survey examined all five cartons, with findings that reconcile against the POD exception line by line. The driver's own delivery note also corroborates torn shrink-wrap on the affected pallet. We understand the photos on file only show three of the five cartons, and we're asking the consignee to check for photos of the remaining two - but given the POD, the inspection, and the driver's note all point the same direction, we don't think the photo gap should be read as an absence of damage, and we'd ask that the remaining units be included in the settlement.

We've reviewed the late-delivery markdown request against our carrier agreement and agree it doesn't fit within the delay terms - we're withdrawing that $18,000.00 component. We'd still like BlueLine to consider the freight charge as a commercial gesture: the shipment arrived four days past the requested date, and both delay events on your tracking record - the terminal backlog and the driver-hours hold - were on BlueLine's side of the operation. We recognize this isn't a contractual claim of right, and we're asking for it as goodwill rather than an entitlement.

Two items are still open on our end. We're checking whether the repack work on the six salvageable units was done in-house or by an outside vendor, and we'll confirm as soon as we have an answer. On packaging, we don't currently have the vendor's packaging specification on file; the inspection report does note that molded foam packaging was present in every carton the inspector opened, which we think speaks to the packaging that was actually used. We can also put together a disposition note on the 14 unsellable units if that would help move things along on your end.

On the piece-count question you raised: our position is that the signed POD, showing 58 of 60 cartons received and countersigned by your consignee's receiving contact at delivery, is the record that should govern the shortage count, rather than the EDI figure. Happy to walk through that further if it would help.

We'd like to close this out at $11,920.00. If it's easier to talk through, I'm glad to get on a call this week. Any settlement we reach here is without prejudice to either side's position on other matters, but let me know if you'd like that noted in writing.

Best,
Maya Chen
Northstar Retail Equipment LLC
